title: NUMERICAL METHODS/ALGORITHMS II (re – numbered from III): On improving un - informed and informed search in Computer Science – including Artificial Intelligence, Logic Programming, and Programming: + iterative Numerical methods (+: Systems (linear, non - linear), Optimization), Programming.).
summary:
in computer science , it is said that most problems reduce to problems of searching and sorting . in artificial intelligence , when a computational agent has a perfect model of its world , 
its problem of reasoning about it s abilities and choosing actions to achieve a goal can 
be abstractly modelled as the mathematical/computer science problem of searching a 
directed graph . 
 this problem is identical (is the dual ) of the problem of looking from 
a start node for a goal node that may or may not be located at the end of one of 
 them ( again with no apriori information ) . a problem that is standard in the searching 
of trees in computer science .    in this paper 
 , we propose a new approach to improving informed and un - informed search in computerscience .  and 
 we show that our approach can be used to improve informed search .
key_findings: Proposed a new approach to improve informed and uninformed search in computer science.
Demonstrated that the new approach enhances the efficiency of informed search.
Established a connection between searching directed graphs and reasoning in artificial intelligence.
methodology: The paper presents a theoretical framework for improving search algorithms, supported by mathematical modeling and analysis.
limitations: The proposed methods may not be applicable to all types of search problems.
Limited empirical validation of the approach across diverse datasets.
Potential computational complexity not fully addressed.
future_work: Explore empirical testing of the proposed methods on various search problems.
Investigate the applicability of the approach in real-world AI applications.
Develop hybrid models that combine informed and uninformed search techniques.
